risk_if_not_implemented: Without Cryptographic Application Programming Interface (API) Abstraction, data in transit and at rest may be exposed through weak, misconfigured or compromised cryptographic protections. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, no risk is rated Likely; risks rated Possible include Reduced Operational Productivity (R-BC-3), Exposure from Unaddressed Vulnerabilities (R-EX-6), Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL) (MT-28), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Secure Engineering Principles
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of industry-recognized security, compliance and resilience practices in the specification, design, development, implementation and modification of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
compensating_control_1.justification: Secure Engineering Principles (SEA-05) provides secure engineering and architectural guidance that compensates for the absence of Cryptographic Application Programming Interface (API) Abstraction (QTS-09.10) by embedding security requirements into design processes as an alternative control mechanism. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to develop applications based on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP).
compensating_control_2.justification: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP) (TDA-05) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Cryptographic Application Programming Interface (API) Abstraction (QTS-09.10) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
